value.rationale: Temporal link persistence is a natural network parameter independently of mean link uptime. The theorem gives a sharp spectral penalty 1/gamma(s), a nontrivial Gumbel deadline law, and an order-n correction to expected complete coverage. Holding stationary availability fixed, the leading penalty continuously ranges from 1 to arbitrarily large values as the switching rate decreases, a structural answer not implied by static coupon collection. The precise invariant is motivated by hub-based coverage under persistent connectivity.
